items.title: Artificial intelligence readiness in healthcare and health professions education in conflict-affected Syria: an online cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly relevant to healthcare delivery, clinical training, and health professions education. Evidence from conflict-affected settings remains limited, despite workforce shortages, disrupted training pathways, and constrained digital infrastructure. This study assessed AI knowledge, trust, willingness, and digital capability among Syrian adults and healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals), with emphasis on implications for AI literacy and professional education. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of Syrian adults from March 4th to May 31st 2026, using a 35-item questionnaire distributed via social media through convenience sampling. The survey assessed AI awareness, trust, willingness, perceived risks and benefits, barriers to healthcare and digital health use, and Digital Literacy. Healthcare respondents (students and qualified professionals) completed additional items on clinical AI use and exposure to unsafe AI recommendations. Composite scores were calculated for AI Trust (3–15), AI Willingness (4–20), and Digital Literacy (2–10). Internal consistency was acceptable to excellent across scales (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.787–0.856). Among 829 participants, 353 (42.6%) were healthcare respondents (119 students and 234 qualified professionals). Mean AI Willingness, AI Trust, and Digital Literacy scores were 14.5 (SD 3.25), 11.0 (SD 2.34), and 6.67 (SD 1.80), respectively. In multivariable linear regression, AI Trust (β = 0.483) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.305) were the strongest predictors, followed by General AI Knowledge (β = 0.165). In sensitivity models excluding the Willingness item that loaded on Trust, Trust (β = 0.44 and 0.38) and Digital Literacy (β = 0.31 and 0.33) remained the strongest correlates. Educational use was the most accepted AI application (65.5%) and educational support was the leading perceived benefit (64.2%). Medical errors were the most frequently perceived risk (76.6%), while cost, unreliable internet access, and lack of Arabic-language content were major implementation barriers. In this online convenience sample, Trust and Digital Literacy were the strongest independent correlates of Willingness to use AI, followed by AI knowledge. The high acceptance of educational AI suggests a practical entry point for conflict-affected health systems. AI literacy should be integrated into undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing health professions education, with explicit training on critical appraisal, safe use, bias, privacy, local validation, and clinician oversight.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Design of High-Temperature High-Entropy Alloys: Progress, Challenges, and Perspectives
items.abstract: High-temperature high-entropy alloys (HTHEAs) provide a large compositional space for tuning phase constitution, microstructure, elevated-temperature strength, creep resistance, and oxidation behavior. Their design is difficult for the same reason: performance depends on processing history, microstructure, temperature, loading mode, exposure time, and environment as well as nominal chemistry. Artificial-intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) methods are increasingly used to navigate this coupled space. This structured narrative review is organized around service-relevant high-temperature evidence rather than algorithm families, covering phase and microstructure stability, elevated-temperature strength, creep, oxidation, and the extent to which AI-selected alloys have been experimentally validated under the intended conditions. Evidence is assessed from internal statistical validation and physics-based filtering to alloy synthesis, direct high-temperature testing, extended service-relevant exposure, and iterative experiment–model feedback. Prospective studies now include tests of model-selected refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) at 800–1200 ∘C, a 149 h creep-rupture validation of an ML-designed high-entropy superalloy (HESA) at 1023 K and 480 MPa, and active-learning campaigns coupled directly to 1000 ∘C oxidation experiments. Across these examples, the limiting factors are concrete: many records lack exposure time, atmosphere, loading mode, measured composition, or post-test microstructure; compression data still outweigh tensile and creep evidence; and few AI-selected alloys have been followed through long-duration service-relevant tests.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Biomarkers for Alzheimer's Disease: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by amyloid-β plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles, necessitating early and accurate diagnosis for effective intervention. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced the discovery and interpretation of AD biomarkers by enabling the integration of complex, multimodal datasets, including neuroimaging, molecular, genetic, and digital biomarkers. AI-driven approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, have demonstrated high accuracy in identifying early pathological changes, predicting disease progression, and distinguishing AD from mild cognitive impairment. Emerging digital biomarkers derived from speech, motor activity, cognitive tests, and wearable sensors further expand non-invasive diagnostic capabilities. Despite promising results, challenges such as data heterogeneity, lack of external validation, limited interpretability ("black-box" models), and difficulties in clinical translation remain substantial barriers. Future research is expected to focus on multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, longitudinal modelling, and personalized prediction frameworks, along with improved standardization and regulatory validation. AI-based biomarker research holds potential to transform early diagnosis, prognosis, and precision medicine in Alzheimer's disease.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based models for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants: a systematic review
items.abstract: Background Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is one of the most common chronic respiratory complications in preterm infants. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential for individualizing preventive strategies and optimizing therapeutic decisions. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models have emerged as promising tools to improve predictive performance in this population. Objective To evaluate and synthesize the predictive performance of AI-based models for BPD development in preterm infants and to assess their methodological quality. Methods A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA recommendations. We searched PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library up to February 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-based models for predicting BPD in preterm infants born at <32 weeks of gestation and/or with a birth weight < 1,500 g were included. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PROBAST tool. Results Eighteen studies were included. Random Forest and XGBoost were the most frequently used algorithms. AUC values for the best-performing models ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, showing improved performance as postnatal variables were incorporated. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high overall risk of bias in 72.2% of the studies, primarily due to deficiencies in the analysis domain. Clinical applicability raised high concern in 38.9% of the studies due to a lack of external validation and heterogeneity in outcome definitions. Conclusions AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation. items.title: Artificial intelligence-driven biomarker discovery and response prediction in cancer immunotherapy: a pan-cancer perspective
items.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed medical oncology, while individual’s therapeutic response to treatment is difficult because of the diverse nature and features of tumors and low precision and accuracy of markers, such as PD-L1, Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB), and Microsatellite Instability (MSI). Artificial intelligence integrates different types of data to cover the complexity of tumor-immune biological mechanisms. This review summarizes the recent studies in AI application in biomarker discovery and cancer immunotherapy prediction from a pan-cancer perspective, summarizing AI techniques, data types, clinical performance metrics, and implementation barriers. Selected AI-derived biomarkers have demonstrated promising performance compared with conventional biomarkers in specific studies. Indeed, selected AI-derived biomarkers demonstrated moderate-to-high discriminatory performance while reported estimates varied according to cancer type, prediction endpoint, and validation design. Deep Learning has shown promising results in Digital Pathology and Radiomics via providing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes quantification and spatial immune phenotyping. Meanwhile, multi-omics integration frameworks, such as graph neural networks and transformer-based models can reveal complex associations among genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data. AI has indicated promising results in predicting both primary and acquired resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors, stratifying potential patients for immunotherapy, and predicting immune-related adverse events. Post-hoc explainability methods, including SHAP and LIME, can provide feature-attribution information, although their outputs should not be interpreted as causal or mechanistic explanations. The intersection of artificial intelligence and cancer immunotherapy is opening new roads for precision-oncology. However, the clinical translation of AI-driven biomarkers requires robust external validation, standardized methodologies, and evaluation across diverse patient populations.
